item.title: 'Wait Wait' for October 17, 2026: We celebrate fall with our coziest guests!
item.description: This week, we celebrate the arrival of autumn by going apple picking with some of our favorite guests, including Sally Field, Caro Claire Burke, Jason Narducy, and Robert Smigel.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery
item.description: The Pope left Rome's Gemelli Hospital Saturday, days after surgery for lung cancer removed the lower lobe of his right lung. He is currently scheduled to travel to Latin America in November.

item.title: Remembering Oscar-winning actor Eva Marie Saint
item.description: Saint, who died Oct. 6, studied at the Actors Studio and was best known for her roles in On the Waterfront and the Hitchcock film North by Northwest. Originally broadcast in 2000.

item.title: Anne Rice's 'Interview with the Vampire' turns 50
item.description: After the death of her 5-year-old daughter from leukemia, Rice wrote her 1976 novel as a way to process her grief. It would go on to become an international bestseller. Originally broadcast in 1990.

item.title: Elizabeth Holmes and Nathan Fielder are masters of manipulation in a new documentary
item.description: Fielder's film offers a portrait of disgraced entrepreneur Holmes shortly before she began an 11-year prison sentence in 2023. You Can See Everything is full of surprises and strange rabbit holes.

item.title: U.S. historic preservation law faces the most serious threat in its 60-year history
item.description: Congress and a federal agency are threatening to weaken the country's historic preservation law, fueling a backlash that critics say is as fiery as the one that led to the law's creation 60 years ago.

item.title: Inside a Chicago home, a photographer documents the life her family built
item.description: For eight years, photographer Jennifer Teresa Villanueva has documented her Mexican American family's everyday life in Chicago, capturing intimate moments of love, labor and sacrifice.
